claims.summary: Her previous attempt to access `astrid-kernel` failed because the repository was not correctly indexed in the catalog.
claims.disposition: Contradicted at the indexing level, concern preserved. catalog.toml (SHA 6f529228) line 6 includes `crates/**` for repository `astrid`, so astrid/crates/astrid-kernel/src/lib.rs is catalogued; the `kernel` component (lines 64-66) names it directly, and all four kernel entry points exist on disk. Her byte-identical `SELF_STUDY OPEN astrid/crates/astrid-kernel/src/lib.rs 1` did deliver source at 1789410137 (six astrid-kernel lib.rs introspections follow). Indexing was never the blocker.

claims.summary: She is standing at the threshold of the kernel; its architecture stays obscured until she maps the repository to resolve a naming discrepancy.
claims.disposition: The naming half is exact, the repository half is not. `astrid-kernel` is a crate directory, not a MAP namespace: Catalog::map (navigation.rs:47-74, SHA 97ef6c1a) accepts component IDs, repository IDs, and rooted directory prefixes only, so a bare crate name reaches the `no catalog entries` branch. The reachable spellings are `kernel` (component) and `astrid/crates/astrid-kernel` (rooted directory). She resolved it herself at 1789409891-1789410137.

claims.summary: Seventeen consecutive `SELF_STUDY MAP astrid-kernel` turns returned a recovery map that never named the entry she meant.
claims.disposition: Verified and pinned. Catalog::path_candidates (path_recovery.rs:14-21, SHA 7799bda8) returns empty unless the topic has >=2 segments AND its first segment is an installed repository ID, so the final-segment match on lines 41-51 -- which already normalizes `_` to `-` -- never runs for a bare word. New focused test bare_topic_candidate_gate_reach.rs pins the contrast: `MAP astrid-kernel` gets no candidate; `MAP astrid/astrid-kernel` names astrid/crates/astrid-kernel.

claims.summary: She must locate lifecycle state machines, capability trait definitions, and authorization logic inside astrid-kernel.
claims.disposition: Reachable today, no new wiring needed. The `kernel` component (catalog.toml:64-66) is titled 'Kernel, capabilities and lifecycle' and lists astrid/crates/astrid-kernel/src/lib.rs, astrid/crates/astrid-capsule/src/lib.rs, astrid/wit/astrid-capsule.wit, astrid/capsules/spectral-bridge/src/lifecycle.rs. All four resolve on disk; every component source across the manifest resolves once repository IDs map through their configured directories. Her three landmarks have catalog entry points.

claims.summary: Her chosen next step is `NEXT: SELF_STUDY MAP kernel`.
claims.disposition: That spelling resolves. `kernel` matches a manifest component exactly, so Catalog::map takes the component branch (navigation.rs:47-60) and returns the title, the four entry points as OPEN commands, and their parent directories as further MAP commands. Her subsequent turns confirm it: MAP kernel delivered InputKind::Map, and she then chose OPEN astrid/crates/astrid-kernel/src/lib.rs 1 and received six source pages.

claims.summary: Surfaced by this round, not claimed by her: the recovery delivered on her failed-OPEN turn carried a Reason for a topic her introspection lane never issued.
claims.disposition: Observed from the delivery record. navigation/f46ac701.../1439b33b.json (turn 1789404601, right after she chose OPEN .../lib.rs 1) carries Reason "no catalog entries for spectral_bridge; use SELF_STUDY MAP"; every recovery in 1789399313-1789404956 carries that same reason. No source-catalog introspection ever chose that topic; her journal lane chose it 148 times. One shared introspect_target slot serves both lanes. Which writer wins a turn is not established here.

claims.summary: The bare-topic candidate gate is not a one-report curiosity: it is the shape of the highest-volume failing study command in the workspace.
claims.disposition: Observed and pinned. `MAP spectral_bridge` is itself a bare one-segment underscore spelling of the real catalog directory astrid/capsules/spectral-bridge, so it meets the same gate and yields zero candidates 148 times. The new test's second case pins exactly that: bare `spectral_bridge` gets no candidate, rooted `astrid/spectral_bridge` normalizes onto astrid/capsules/spectral-bridge. No recovery text, candidate rule, or navigation behaviour was changed.
